title: Made a Diablo 2 clone with auto play and 16 different classes…
author: batmessiah
selftext:
This is my first attempt at making a full game, which I’m calling VELSCOUR.  You can play it in your browser on desktop or mobile (Add to Home Screen for best experience) The game has procedurally generated dungeons, and you’re effectively trying to make it to floor 500, so you can kill VELSCOUR, the game’s namesake, whatever he is.  What you do know is that every time you level up, VELSCOUR taunts you from the 500th floor…

Most of the sprite work was done in ChatGPT with Claude Code doing most of the heavy lifting.  Used up my weekly sub quotas, but the main meat of the game is there.  Be sure to hit “auto” (upper right near the map) to get the game started in auto mode to see lots of fancy stuff happen.  My favorite classes are Dragoon, Slime Lord, Lancer, and Paladin so far.  My mind is still blown that I was able to make this with prompts and some examples over a few days with 2 $20 subscriptions.

replies.author: SoonBlossom
replies.body: How do you do that ? I'm new to Claude, I was using imagegen from chatGPT before to make sprites and sprite sheets for animations but it's lonnggggg

replies.author: FazedEclipse2
replies.body:
You need something beyond the initial idea BUT my first prompt was basically:

Imagine a diablo 2 clone built in code drawn pixel art, the main characters are JRPG archetypes as are the enemies

And from that prompt slimebane was born. It made the game in minutes, it had 5 acts 5 bosses and procedurally generated dungeons.

What it lacked was the inner workings.

I've said in another post...those inner workings are freely available.

replies.author: FazedEclipse2
replies.body:
With regards your sprites. I can't currently show you an example, but if you use Imagegen to generate a four direction sprite (sideways not isometric, front and back) then ask it to build it in blender to render down with as much detail as possible, you can generate very good sprite work. It's animated, it makes the sprite sheets itself.

It just works

replies.author: TheFish77
replies.body: My biggest piece of advice is to specify as much as possible. Give it word docs, spreadsheets, context etc. Think of it as translating ideas into code. It just doesn't know what it doesn't know.

replies.author: batmessiah
replies.body: EXACTLY.  I wrote out a 4 page long prompt and attached some of the first sprite sets to produce the first iteration of the game.  45 pushed iterations later, and this is the result.  I've even updated it since I posted this last night.  There's no longer any placeholder art in the game.

replies.author: batmessiah
replies.body: Well, 2 x $20 subs, but yeah, I learned A LOT.  It wasn't easy to make, but it wasn't hard either.  Lots of prompts, the first one was 5 pages long.  Having ChatGPT making and re-using rigging to keep the walls/art consistent was a game changer as well.

It's interesting how well it works, because the town layout is procedurally generated for each new character.  All the dungeon levels are procedurally generated.
